about_the_game:
Escape Simulator - A Ridiculous and Exciting Physical Escape Journey

You are tied to a creaking wooden chair and placed in a cold concrete dungeon. This is not a traditional escape game - you are manipulating the chair itself! By precisely controlling the four legs of the chair (Q/E/A/D keys correspond to legs 7, 9, 1, and 3 respectively), experience an unprecedented absurd survival experience: long press the Q key to support only one leg, and lift the other three legs in the air, instantly transforming the chair into a fragile tumbler.

Rotation is the only way to move: the left button is counterclockwise, the right button is clockwise, and the point where the chair legs touch is the axis of rotation. When landing on multiple legs, carefully swing forward with the pivot center as the center. Activate the automatic save point of the radiation pattern along the way - wait for the progress bar to fill up, here are your new respawn coordinates. Mistakes and falls? Press and hold the R key for 2 seconds to reset to full health!

From a flat warehouse to a dangerous kidnapper's lair, seven levels test your balance art:

▶ Starting on flat ground, familiar with basic swing

▶ Bypass right angle bends and deep pit traps

▶ Be cautious of tipping over when conquering slopes

▶ Repeatedly adjusting the center of gravity in convex terrain

▶ The instantaneous heartbeat acceleration of leaping over the high-low platform

The low polygon realistic style combines retro film noise and high saturation tones, making the sparks of chair leg friction particularly dazzling in dark scenes. Every shake is accompanied by metal moans and rapid breathing, and the faint light shining outside the finish line door is the ultimate redemption for your solitary survival.

short_description: Control a worn-out wooden chair that is tied up to the victim Q. The E, A, and D keys respectively accurately lift specific chair legs, and the left and right keys drive rotation and swinging forward. When using one leg as the axis, the nerves need to be tightened to maintain balance.
